case_studies.title: ElasticBack: Stealthy Conditional Backdoor in LLM-Agent Skills via Coupled Trigger-Rule Optimization
case_studies.abstract: Agent skills, bundles of instructions and resources that an LLM agent loads on demand, form an emerging supply chain where a single poisoned skill can persistently compromise every agent that installs it. However, existing skill attacks either fire on every request or rely on fine-tuned weights or multiple skills, leaving a conditional and low-cost backdoor unexplored. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of creating a stealthy backdoor in large language model (LLM) agent skills, by building a system called ElasticBack that can plant a malicious rule in a skill document and a trigger in a user query. The result is a conditional backdoor that can compromise an LLM agent without being easily detected. This research is relevant to IT security and artificial intelligence applications.

This flags a risk: if your org uses LLM agents with installable skills, check your security protocols immediately. Not directly applicable to general cloud infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: Security Tests as Executable Specifications for LLM Code Generation: Benefits, Trade-offs, and Coverage Limits
case_studies.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) can generate functionally useful code that remains vulnerable, while security-focused interventions may break intended behavior. We investigate security tests as executable specifications both before generation and during iterative repair. We develop SecTDD, a controlled test-feedback scaffold that separates three factors: whether tests are shown upfront, whether failed executions trigger revision, and how failures are selected and represented. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of ensuring security in code generated by large language models, building a framework called SecTDD to integrate security tests into the code generation process, and resulting in more secure code. The SecTDD framework allows for iterative repair of generated code based on failed security tests. This project focuses on code generation security, which may be relevant to IT teams using automated coding tools.
case_studies.it_breakdown: If you manage cloud infrastructure that uses automated coding tools, here is what to do: review your current code generation process for security vulnerabilities, consider integrating security tests into your workflow, and evaluate the use of frameworks like SecTDD to improve code security.

case_studies.title: SHE: Trajectory-driven Safety Harness Evolution for LLM Agents
case_studies.abstract: The safety of large language model (LLM) agents depends not only on model weights but also on the agent harness that manages context, memory, tools, permissions, and runtime control. Existing safety mechanisms often treat the harness as a fixed deployment artifact, limiting their ability to evolve with emerging risks. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of evolving safety mechanisms for large language model agents by building a framework called Safety Harness Evolution. case_studies.title: Consilience for Verifier-Free Test-Time Scaling
case_studies.abstract: Test-time scaling often uses an external verifier, such as compilers and test cases in coding or trained value functions in robotics applications, to obtain high-quality rollouts. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of test-time scaling in Large Language Models without using external verifiers, by building a confidence-based verifier-free test-time scaling method, which results in more accurate rollouts. The method computes and ranks rollouts solely by confidence, eliminating the need for high-quality verifiers. This advancement enhances the reasoning capabilities of Large Language Models in real-world applications.

case_studies.abstract: Automated Text-to-Speech (TTS) evaluation methods (Mean Opinion Score (MOS) predictors and Audio Large Language Models (Audio-LLM) judges) are expected to reflect human perception, yet it is unclear how well they capture the distinct aspects of speech that listeners actually perceive. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of automated text-to-speech evaluation methods not accurately reflecting human perception by breaking down 'naturalness' into 10 distinct dimensions. The result provides a more accurate way to evaluate automated text-to-speech systems.

case_studies.title: Software Engineering for and with GUI Agent
case_studies.abstract: GUI agents have advanced rapidly, producing a growing body of frameworks, benchmarks, and applications. However, this growth has outpaced the maturity of the field. GUI agents remain technically brittle, incompletely engineered, and insufficiently validated for sustained real-world use. They are evolving into closed-loop software systems. Within these systems, model reasoning is coupled with interface perception, execution feedback, recovery, and human oversight. case_studies.summary: This research aims to improve the reliability of GUI agents by applying software engineering principles to their development. The authors built a framework to address the technical brittleness and lack of validation in GUI agents. The result is a more robust and sustainable approach to GUI agent development.

case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of on-policy distillation in large language models, where students can achieve high token agreement with teachers despite producing flawed responses. The authors built a new approach that focuses on teacher-student mismatch, categorizing mismatch tokens into two types. The result is a more effective on-policy distillation method, but it's not directly relevant to IT infrastructure work.

case_studies.title: ColluSkill: Adversarial Cross-Skill Composition for Evading Agent Skill Scanners
case_studies.abstract: Agent skills are emerging as an important attack surface in LLM-based agent systems. Through an empirical study of existing skill scanners, we find that current defenses mainly inspect individual skills, leaving risks from cross-skill composition insufficiently examined. This creates a practical blind spot: multiple locally plausible skills may pass security checks while collectively forming a harmful workflow during agent execution. case_studies.summary: This research solves the problem of identifying potential security risks in agent systems by composing multiple skills that can collectively form a harmful workflow. The authors built ColluSkill, a framework that can decompose a malicious intent into interdependent skills that may pass individual security checks. The result highlights a blind spot in current defenses that inspect individual skills only.
